name: thinkphp-lang-include-execute
notes: The execution half of `include`, and it exists because the obvious route
does not work on a default build. A wrapper carrying code -- `data://`,
`php://input` -- needs allow_url_include, which PHP has defaulted off since
5.2 and which the php/inclusion target refused in its own words. What works
is to make the sink include PEAR's own command-line script and hand that
script arguments through the query string: `config-create` writes its output
to a path the arguments name, and the code goes in the output.
Two things about the shape were measured rather than reasoned.
The payload is the WHOLE query string, not one parameter's value.
register_argc_argv builds argv from the query string, so `config-create` and
the target filename have to sit outside the parameter carrying the
traversal. That is why the invocation marks `?FUZZ` and passes
`--verify-url-location raw`: percent-encoding the payload would turn the `&`
that separates those arguments into data and the write would never happen.
And the proof is the second request, not the first. The write answers 200
whether or not anything was interpreted, so the verdict comes from fetching
the written file back: measured, the fetch returned 11688702 for 6022*1941
with the source form `<?=6022*1941?>` absent, which is the difference
between a file that was interpreted and one served verbatim. The same
distinction `write` has drawn since 2.31.0, and this method reports it the
same way -- `file-write` for the verbatim case.
The control is a tier ceiling and it was chosen by measurement, not taste.
The obvious control was `--methods reflected` on the same URL, and it is the
wrong one: measured, it sends 37 probes and 32 of them come back `error`,
because a shell payload sent raw into a query string breaks the request
before it arrives. A control whose probes mostly never reach the target says
nothing about false confirmation, which is why the runner refuses `error` as
an expectation at all.
So the control removes the one thing the proof rests on and keeps everything
else: the same vulnerable build, the same risk tier, the same probes, with
no --include-write-url. Measured, 16 probes reach the target and all 16 come
back `negative`. That is the statement worth pinning -- the execution
verdict comes from reading the written file back, and without somewhere to
read it from this method does not reach `executed` on a target where it
otherwise does.
